methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents institutional capacity-building outside metro hubs, creating peer networks for AI fluency in a traditionally non-tech region—exactly the distributed deep learning infrastructure that enables Build It Yourself scenarios.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA concentrates educational resources and innovation capacity in Richmond's metro core, deepening existing regional advantages while leaving the distribution question unresolved—will this knowledge radiate outward or accumulate inward?

signals.title: VT Science Corner: Designing better battery technology with X-rays and AI - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's AI-driven battery research demonstrates deep technical capability anchored to institutional presence, but specialized research excellence doesn't automatically translate to broad workforce capability across the region—classic concentrated depth pattern.

signals.title: How are AI use and policy changing in schools? New VCU research identifies key gaps - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU research identifying gaps in school AI policy reveals shallow, reactive adoption patterns across Virginia schools—institutions are using AI tools without developing deep understanding or coherent frameworks, signaling broad but superficial distribution.

signals.title: By water use, Google’s Botetourt site would be its 8th largest data center complex in the world
signals.signal_reading: Google's massive data center in Botetourt extracts regional resources (water, power, tax incentives) while providing primarily infrastructure jobs rather than AI capability development—economic presence without knowledge transfer widens rather than bridges capability gaps.
